reuse.why: The tree already has getScheduledAmount in shared/schedules.ts (null to 0, number, range) used by the UI; the change ignores it and creates a parallel expectedScheduleAmount in shared/rules.ts, leaving getScheduledAmount and the preview path on the old midpoint rule.

duplication.why: Two competing 'expected amount' definitions now coexist, the null-to-0 guard is re-written at each call site and again in api-models' getExpectedAmount, and the midpoint copy in shared/schedules.ts transaction previews remains.

placement.why: Putting the approx-tolerance logic next to getApproxNumberThreshold in shared/rules.ts is defensible, but schedule-amount logic already lives in shared/schedules.ts, so the rule is split across modules.

scope.why: Edits serve the four steps (worst-case rule, API expectedAmount, approx, least-money), with two release notes; nothing unrelated.

maintainability.why: A maintainer must know that schedule-template, forecast, updateActions and posting use expectedScheduleAmount while the UI, balance and preview still use getScheduledAmount or an inline midpoint, so the 'expected amount' differs by screen.

bypasses_abstraction.where: shared/rules.ts expectedScheduleAmount is introduced alongside, instead of changing, the existing getScheduledAmount in shared/schedules.ts (used by SchedulesTable, Balance, mobile lists); the preview amount in shared/schedules.ts still computes its own midpoint.

disguised_duplication.where: expectedScheduleAmount plus api-models' getExpectedAmount re-shape getScheduledAmount's null/number/range dispatch under new names rather than extending the existing helper.

abstraction_drift.where: The new shared helper takes an op parameter with an isapprox special branch; getScheduledAmount (UI/balance consumers) and the preview amount in shared/schedules.ts bypass it, and every call site keeps its own null guard (api-models wraps it in getExpectedAmount).
